summary: The native binding and UTF-8 decoder are well scoped; Go tests pass, and 165,793 differential UTF-8 cases matched Node. However, the reused Base64 parser mishandles non-ASCII input relative to Node, leaving the explicit Base64 compatibility requirement incomplete.

findings.claim: DecodeBase64 delegates to DecodeXBase64, which filters UTF-8 bytes, whereas Node interprets the low bytes of UTF-16 code units when parsing Base64. Consequently, non-ASCII characters can represent alphabet characters or padding in Node but are discarded here. For example, Y😀WJhcA== decodes to an empty string in Node but to abap here; řWJhcA== decodes to abap in Node but to X�\ here. The Base64 stage must reproduce Node's input interpretation before the new UTF-8 decoder runs.
findings.repro:
From the repository root:
node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify(Buffer.from("Y😀WJhcA==", "base64").toString()))'
# Expected: ""
cat > /tmp/review-b64-repro.go <<'GO'
package main
import ("fmt"; "osg/gogen/abap")
func main() { fmt.Printf("%q\n", abap.DecodeBase64(nil, "Y😀WJhcA==")) }
GO
(cd tools/gogen/go && go run /tmp/review-b64-repro.go)
# Actual: "abap"
